name: Tenancy
purpose: Resolves which organization a request belongs to, and keeps every other tenant's rows unreachable. The layer every other module sits on.
features: Host header → organization lookup, Redis-cached with negative caching for unknown hosts
`withTenant(ctx, …)` / `forTenant(ctx)` set transaction-local Postgres session vars, so a pooled connection cannot leak context between requests
`setTenantContext()` adopts an organization mid-transaction, for registration only
`withUserIdentity()` reads only the caller's own `memberships` rows, pre-tenant
`assertRlsActive()` refuses to boot the app on an owner (RLS-bypassing) connection
Self-serve registration: organization + domain + first branch + owner + membership + ORG_OWNER grant + trial subscription in one transaction
userActions: Register a clinic from the apex domain (4-step signup with live slug availability)
Be provisioned by a platform admin, optionally converting a demo request
businessRules: BR-TEN-001
BR-TEN-002
BR-TEN-003
BR-TEN-004
BR-TEN-005
limitations: Custom domains are modelled (`organization_domains.isPlatformSub`) but there is no verification flow
`organizations` and `organization_domains` are deliberately outside RLS — the host→tenant lookup cannot require the context it establishes
Slug availability is a customer-list oracle by construction; mitigated only by rate limiting

name: Authentication
purpose: Proves who a caller is and issues the session they act under. Password and phone-OTP, refresh rotation with reuse detection.
features: Password login by email or phone, constant-time failure, one message for every cause including 'not a member here'
Phone OTP: hashed at rest, single-use, attempt-capped
Access token is a 15-minute stateless JWT; refresh token is an opaque 256-bit string stored only as a SHA-256 hash
Refresh rotation — replaying a rotated token revokes the whole family
Account lockout after 5 failed attempts
Branch and organization switching without re-authenticating
Sessions in httpOnly host-only cookies; Next is the BFF, tokens never reach client JS
userActions: Sign in with a password or a one-time code
Switch active branch or organization
Sign out
businessRules: BR-AUTH-001
BR-AUTH-002
BR-AUTH-003
BR-AUTH-004
BR-AUTH-005
BR-AUTH-006
limitations: OTP delivery is a logging stub behind `services/notification/sender.ts`, pending TRAI DLT registration
`emailVerifiedAt` is never set — there is no email verification flow
`user_identities` exists for SSO but no provider is wired

name: IAM
purpose: Who may do what, where. Roles cloned from the system set, granted per branch or clinic-wide, with per-person exceptions.
features: Resolution order DENY > GRANT > role grants, branch-scoped, with validity windows
A NULL `branch_id` on a `membership_roles` row means every branch in the organization
Custom roles are clones of read-only system roles; a database trigger stops a tenant shadowing a system role code
Per-person GRANT/DENY overrides on top of role defaults
Member suspension and restoration
Three privilege-escalation guards in `services/iam/guards.ts` (STATUS.md says four; the file header says three)
userActions: Create a custom role by cloning a system role
Grant or take away a role, for one branch or all
Add or clear a per-person permission exception
Suspend or restore a colleague
businessRules: BR-IAM-001
BR-IAM-002
BR-IAM-003
BR-IAM-004
BR-IAM-005
BR-IAM-006
BR-IAM-007
limitations: The escalation guards are application-level only — the database does not enforce them, and two of them cannot be, because the database has no idea what its caller is allowed to do. A direct SQL write bypasses them
Resolved access is cached in Redis; every write must call `invalidateUserAccess` or a revoked role keeps working until the TTL

name: Branches
purpose: The places a clinic operates from. One organization, one or many branches — a solo clinic and a hospital group are the same shape.
features: Branch CRUD with a tenant-qualified `code`
Weekly operating hours with per-day slot minutes
Closure dates
Soft delete via `deletedAt`, never a boolean
userActions: Open a branch
Edit branch details and GST number
Set the opening-hours week strip
Retire a branch
businessRules: BR-BR-001
BR-BR-002
BR-BR-003
limitations: Closures are modelled but no screen manages them
`branch_operating_hours` and `branch_closures` have no `organization_id`; they are protected by a parent-scoped RLS policy through `branches`

name: Invitations
purpose: How a colleague gets into a clinic. Issue, revoke, resend, and an unauthenticated accept page.
features: Token hashed at rest, same treatment as a refresh token
Invitation carries the role and the branches it will grant
Revoke and resend
Unauthenticated `/join` page that creates the user, membership and role grant on accept
userActions: Invite someone by email or phone, choosing role and branches
Revoke or resend a pending invitation
Accept an invitation and set a password
businessRules: BR-INV-001
BR-INV-002
BR-INV-003
BR-INV-004
limitations: Delivery is the same logging stub as OTP — the invitation link is only visible in the API logs
No expiry sweep; expired invitations are filtered at read time, never deleted

name: Patients
purpose: The people being treated. The first PHI in the product: identity is org-wide so a duplicate can be found before it is created, attendance is branch-local, and every read is recorded in `data_access_logs`.
features: Registration issuing an org-wide UHID and a branch-local MRN through `issueNumber`, gapless and concurrency-safe
Duplicate detection on phone, ABHA, national id, and name+date-of-birth together — org-wide, across branches the caller cannot see
Trigram search over name and phone, plus exact UHID and MRN, scoped to the caller's branches or widened to the organization
Allergies, problems and medicines behind a separate `patient.medical_history.*` permission
Address and next of kin, with a guardian flag distinct from the emergency contact
Age recorded as a birth date OR a stated approximation, never both
userActions: Search for a patient by name, phone or number
Register a new patient at a clinic
Register an existing patient at a second clinic
Open a patient record and read the chart
Record and withdraw an allergy, a problem or a medicine
Stop a medicine
limitations: ⚠️ `patients` carries NO `branch_isolation` policy, deliberately — the branch boundary is on `patient_registrations`. See ADR-0016 before 'fixing' it
`patient_allergies.medicine_id` and `patient_conditions.diagnosis_id` are absent until the Phase 5 catalogues exist; both carry free text instead
No merge flow yet. `status = MERGED` and `merged_into_id` exist, tied together by a CHECK, and nothing writes them
Family history, insurances, documents and consents from the §6 ERD are not built
`patients.status = DECEASED` and `deceased_on` are storable but no screen sets them

name: Appointments
purpose: Booking, and the availability engine behind it. PHI: a patient, a doctor and a reason disclose more together than any one of them. Unlike `patients`, `appointments` IS branch-scoped — identity follows the person, attendance belongs to the clinic it happened at.
features: One availability engine every booking path goes through — recurring blocks, APPROVED exceptions, EXTRA_SHIFT, branch closures, past slots and the advisory per-block cap
Slot length resolved through the single chain of ADR-0015; the engine imports `effectiveSlotMinutes` rather than re-deriving it
Every wall-clock to instant conversion done in Postgres with an explicit `::timestamp` cast, never in Node
Double-booking refused by a GiST EXCLUDE constraint whose predicate excludes CANCELLED and NO_SHOW, so cancelling frees the slot with no release step
A transition map in the service and CHECK constraints in the database; NO_SHOW is unreachable after a check-in
Branch-local appointment numbers from `issueNumber`, issued immediately before the insert so the counter lock is one statement wide
Booking registers the patient at the branch on their first visit there, reusing the MRN issue
An append-only status trail, by the same owner-exempt trigger plus REVOKE as `audit_logs`
userActions: See which slots are free for a doctor on a day
Book an appointment against a free slot
Move a booking to another time or another doctor
Check a patient in, start the consultation, mark it seen
Cancel a booking with a stated reason
Record that a patient did not attend
Read one booking and its status trail
limitations: ⚠️ `appointment_status_history` RESTATES the branch predicate from `appointments`. RLS is NOT applied inside a policy expression's subquery, so it cannot be inherited — change one and change the other
The engine cannot see a booking for the same doctor at a branch outside the caller's scope, and must not. The EXCLUDE constraint catches it and the 409 never names who holds the slot
`maxPatients` is advisory — two concurrent bookings into different free slots can take a block one over its cap
A reschedule writes no status-history row; the move is in `audit_logs` only
No queue tokens, no walk-in flow — Stage 5. `QUEUE_TOKEN` numbering exists and nothing writes it
Nothing sends a reminder; `appointment.reminder_hours_before` is seeded and no worker reads it
The day board deliberately writes no `data_access_logs` row — see the service header before adding one

name: Audit
purpose: An append-only record of who changed what. Ids and permission codes only — never a name, never PHI.
features: Structured before/after diff of the changed fields
Actor, organization, branch, action and target on every row
Written inside the same transaction as the change it records
businessRules: BR-AUD-001
BR-AUD-002
limitations: No viewer — rows are only readable via SQL
`data_access_logs` for PHI reads is planned but does not exist
Nothing enforces append-only at the database level; it is a convention

name: PlatformConsole
purpose: What the platform operator sees. Demo-request pipeline, provisioning, and eventually impersonation.
features: Demo-request list with status pipeline
Provision an organization from a demo request or from scratch
Platform admin login, separate from any tenant
userActions: Review incoming demo requests
Provision a clinic
Sign in to the platform console at the `admin.` subdomain
businessRules: BR-PLT-001
BR-PLT-002
limitations: Impersonation is not implemented. The session it mints must carry a real branch scope — a platform admin has no membership, so `loadUserAccess` returns null and every branch-scoped write would be refused
No plan or subscription management screens

name: Marketing
purpose: The apex domain. Landing page, signup, legal pages and the demo form — everything that happens before a tenant exists.
features: Landing page: hero, six-station journey rail, modules, multi-branch, isolation, India-first, pricing, demo form
The design system every later screen inherits — surgical-green palette, IBM Plex, spacing and radius scale, in `apps/web/src/app/globals.css`
4-step signup with live slug availability checking
Demo form: rate-limited, honeypot plus timing check, silent discard, deduplicated
Measured accessibility pass — 4.5:1 contrast, 24×24 targets, skip link, rail pause control, `aria-describedby` on every field
userActions: Read about the product
Book a demo
Register a clinic
Read the privacy policy, terms and DPA
businessRules: BR-MKT-001
BR-MKT-002
limitations: Legal pages are unreviewed drafts with ~30 unfilled placeholders and a visible 'not yet in force' banner
`src/lib/analytics.ts` is a no-op seam pending a DPDP consent decision
No real OG image; footer brand facts are placeholders
Screen-reader behaviour in a real AT and the OS reduced-motion toggle are implemented but never exercised end to end

name: Notifications
purpose: The seam every outbound message goes through. Real logic, no delivery.
features: One `sender.ts` seam for OTP codes and invitation links
Logs the message instead of sending it
businessRules: BR-NOT-001
limitations: Nothing is delivered. Blocked on TRAI DLT registration for SMS and Meta template approval for WhatsApp
No notification templates table, no provider abstraction, no delivery-status tracking

name: Worker
purpose: Background jobs on BullMQ. Every queue is registered; the billing clock and invoice PDF rendering are implemented, the rest are stubs.
features: Redis connection and queue registration, defined in `@rcln/queue` — a package because a queue has TWO ends and the API is now a producer

Job payloads are a WIRE FORMAT across a rolling deploy: plain JSON, ids only, never PHI. A payload sits in Redis, is echoed into every failure log line, and stays in the dead-letter queue for seven days
The billing clock — an hourly repeatable sweep fanning out one job per subscription
Invoice PDF rendering — Chromium in THIS container and never in the api, which is capped at 1g and already exits 137 running its own test suite
Document rendering runs at concurrency 1, because each job holds a renderer process
`jobId.invoicePdf(id, attempt)` — BullMQ de-duplicates on job id even for a RECENTLY COMPLETED job, which is right for a double-clicked button and silently wrong for a deliberate regeneration

The expiry sweep — an hourly repeatable job that moves expired stock out of AVAILABLE. HOURLY rather than nightly because "midnight" is a different instant in every clinic: each tick asks every branch whether the date has rolled over IN ITS OWN ZONE
It shares the ledger writer with the API through `@rcln/inventory` rather than writing its own INSERT — PI-ADR-004's "only one writer" is what forced the engine into a package
limitations: Notifications, reports, integrations and outbox accept jobs that nothing consumes. The inventory queue now has a processor
No dead-letter handling and no metrics rollup
A render that fails all five attempts leaves the invoice with no current document and nothing asks again
`InvoicePdfJob.requestedBy` is required, so a future non-human producer has to decide what actor to record rather than defaulting one

name: Contracts
purpose: Zod schemas shared by API and web. The request/response shape is written once and both sides import it.
features: Validation and inferred TypeScript types from the same declaration
Grouped by domain: common, auth, tenancy, marketing
limitations: No runtime response validation on the web side — contracts type the response but nothing parses it
Chosen over tRPC/ts-rest deliberately; revisit if a mobile client appears

name: Documents
purpose: Stores, retrieves and RENDERS every document the platform holds. One provider interface for the bytes (local disk in development, a private S3 bucket in production, nothing above the seam knows which) and one template function for the look — where the SAME function produces the on-screen preview and the printed PDF, so the two cannot drift.
features: `StorageProvider` — put / get / head / exists / remove / getSignedUrl, and deliberately nothing else
`LocalStorageProvider` — atomic write-then-rename, a metadata sidecar so content type is never sniffed from the extension, and three independent layers stopping a key escaping the storage root
`createStorageProvider()` — the single place `STORAGE_PROVIDER` is read; selecting s3 fails loudly rather than falling back to local disk

`DocumentService` — generic over `DocumentType`, so lab reports and prescriptions land here without editing it. Lives in `@rcln/documents/store` because the WORKER writes a document and the API serves it
Row → bytes → READY ordering, so a failed render leaves evidence rather than a document the system swears exists and cannot serve
SHA-256 recorded by the provider over what it actually wrote, and verified again on every read

`renderInvoiceHtml(data)` — ONE function, TWO destinations: an `<iframe srcdoc>` preview in apps/web and Chromium's `setContent` in the worker. That is the whole guarantee that the screen and the PDF are the same document
The rendered HTML is self-contained — inlined CSS, inlined typefaces, NOT ONE external request. `page.pdf()` snapshots what is painted, so a font still in flight is a PDF silently set in the fallback

IBM Plex Sans/Mono vendored as base64 constants (`latin` + `latin-ext`, which is where ₹ lives) rather than read from node_modules, because every failure of a runtime read is silent in one of the three runtimes
`playwright-core` driving the DISTRIBUTION's Chromium in the worker — one browser per process, one context per job
`invoice_documents.template_key` / `.template_version` — provenance, so a disputed reprint years later can be explained
limitations: The S3 provider is designed but not implemented — `STORAGE_PROVIDER=s3` is a fatal boot error until phase 11 of the invoice engine

⚠️ `files`' RLS policy permits a NULL `organization_id` for platform assets, so the explicit `organizationId` pin in `getDocument` is the ONLY thing stopping a tenant reading a platform-owned document — `db:rls:check` can never notice its removal
⚠️ `getSignedUrl` returns null on local disk by design; the download route must be able to stream bytes itself, and a signed URL is an optimisation rather than a boundary

⚠️ Non-Latin scripts (Devanagari, Tamil, Kannada…) render as missing-glyph boxes — the vendored subsets are Latin. The render job LOGS the script name, never the characters, so the gap is known rather than silent. The fix is another `@font-face`
⚠️ The Alpine Chromium moves with the base image, not with the lockfile, so a layout regression can arrive from a `docker build` with no dependency change
No route serves a PDF and no screen renders the preview — phases 7 and 9
No sweep for rows stuck in GENERATING, and no sweep that retries a render that failed its five attempts
No delete path

name: Tax
purpose: Decides whether an issuer may charge tax on a supply at all, and only then at what rate. One set of rules, two issuers: rcln billing a clinic for its subscription, and a clinic billing a patient.
features: `resolveTax()` — starts from "do we hold a registration here?", never from "what rate?", and returns NOT_REGISTERED with the reason on the document when nothing covers the place of supply
`placeOfSupply` as an explicit input — the customer's location for a digital service (a subscription), the issuing BRANCH for a service performed at a place (a consultation)
`tax_rules` — effective-dated rates per item tax category, carrying the LINE NAME and split behaviour so the presentation is data rather than an assumption about India

`tax_rule_defaults` — the rate cards rcln maintains per country, INHERITED at read time and never copied into a tenant, so a published rate change reaches every clinic that has not overridden it with one INSERT

Precedence: a tenant rule beats a platform default before specificity is considered, all-or-nothing per tax category — the clinic signs the return, and a half-inherited rate card is one nobody authored

`rulesFor()` returns every applicable rule — a regional rule normally overrides the country-wide one, but a `stacks` rule adds to it, which is the only way Canada's federal GST + provincial PST can be billed at all
India's CGST/SGST/IGST split is one rule with `split: INTRA_STATE_HALVES`; every other GST country prints one line, and `regionalLineName` covers UTGST
`TaxProviderQuote` — the seam for US sales tax and EU One Stop Shop; the engine stays pure and prices from the provider's own lines, or returns PROVIDER_REQUIRED
`UNRATED` / `PROVIDER_REQUIRED` — a category with no rule, or a regime no table can compute, charges nothing and says so rather than borrowing a rate
`UNISSUABLE_TREATMENTS` + `isIssuable()` — the shared list so the engine and Phase 5's finalisation guard cannot drift
`loadTaxContext()` — one read per invoice, after which pricing every line is pure
businessRules: Tax may only be charged where the issuer holds a registration covering the place of supply; an empty registration set means nothing is ever taxed
A clinical service is supplied at the branch that performed it, never at the patient's home address
The rate is a property of the item, not of the registration — a clinic's registration carries no standard rate at all
What a tax line is CALLED is a property of the rule, not of the country: Ontario prints one HST line and British Columbia prints GST plus PST
A stacked regional tax is charged on the net, never on the net plus the federal tax — that would be a tax on a tax
A rate change is a new effective-dated row, never an edit, so an issued invoice stays explicable
Removing a tax rule is an end date, never a delete — the row that priced an issued invoice is what explains it to an auditor
Only healthcare-service exemptions are seeded; goods rates vary by product within a country, so an unverified default would be wrong invisibly for every clinic in it
limitations: No platform console SCREEN for the defaults catalogue — the four routes exist but are curl-only until phase 7
No tenant-facing screen or permission for a clinic's own registrations and overrides — phase 7
The divergence warning that makes tenant-beats-platform safe needs a screen to live on, so it does not exist yet
⚠️ Canada is fully supported by the engine and tested, but is absent from `locale.ts`, so no clinic can select it at signup
⚠️ Goods are deliberately unseeded, so a clinic billing medicines gets UNRATED until it configures rates it has checked
⚠️ UNRATED and PROVIDER_REQUIRED lines are reported, not refused — the finalisation guard that must not ISSUE them is phase 5
No tax provider is implemented, so US sales tax and EU cross-border consumer VAT charge nothing; the seam takes a quote but nothing fills it
A customer tax id is always UNVALIDATED — no VIES or GSTIN validation path, so a B2B invoice cannot reach reverse charge
Seeded defaults are a starting point with provenance, not tax advice — each needs a per-country review before billing

name: Invoicing
purpose: The clinic billing a PATIENT: one engine, many billable sources, the clinic's own registration, immutable once issued. ⚠️ NOT `subscription_invoices`, which is rcln billing the clinic and is complete — see §0.1 of the invoice-engine log for why the two cannot share a table.
features: `invoices` / `invoice_items` / `invoice_taxes` / `invoice_documents` — org AND branch scoped, composite-FK'd throughout
`issueInvoiceNumber()` — `INV-{PERIOD_YEAR}-{SOURCE}-{BRANCH_CODE}-{000001}` on top of the existing gapless `issueNumber()` counter
The reset cadence is resolved from the branch's country — financial year for IN, calendar year elsewhere — and the period is the BRANCH-LOCAL date, resolved in Postgres
Every tax field on an invoice is a snapshot: registration number, legal name, place of supply, line names, rates. Nothing is ever re-read

One TYPED, enforced reference column per integrated source — `appointment_id` today, `lab_order_id` and `pharmacy_sale_id` with their modules — never a generic polymorphic id. `source_type` still ships as the full seven-value enum so the shape does not change when they land
`priceInvoice()` in `@rcln/invoicing` — the ONLY code allowed to decide what goes in a money column. Pure: integer minor units, no Prisma, no clock, `quoteTax` passed in as a function

The calculation order is fixed once and implemented once: gross → line discount → apportioned invoice discount → per-line tax → cash rounding, each step rounded at the currency's own scale before the next reads it
`apportion()` — largest-remainder split of the invoice-level discount pro-rata by taxable amount, ties broken on the lower index so a reprint matches the original exactly
Quantity is an integer count of THOUSANDTHS, matching `Decimal(14,3)` — a float unit price is how a line comes out a paisa short of the sum of its parts
Cash rounding is applied to the TOTAL and never to a line, and lands in its own column so `grand_total` never needs explaining
`priceDraftInvoice()` — the seam: one tax-context read per invoice, then pure arithmetic. Persists nothing; finalisation is phase 5
`createDraftInvoice()` / `repriceDraftInvoice()` — a draft is PRICED from the moment it exists; there is no state in which an invoice's totals are not the totals of its lines
`finalizeInvoice()` — price, refuse an unrated line, refuse a branch its registration does not cover, then take the number: DRAFT → FINALIZING → ISSUED in one transaction
`cancelDraftInvoice()` / `voidInvoice()` — cancel is for a draft nobody ever saw, void is for a document that keeps its number for ever
Three database triggers, not one service: `invoices_lifecycle_guard` (the transition table + a frozen-column ALLOW-LIST), `invoices_no_delete_after_issue`, `invoice_children_follow_parent`
The frozen set is an allow-list, so a column added to `invoices` tomorrow is immutable after issue by default and somebody has to argue for it
`toDecimal()` / `toMoney()` — the ONE `numeric(14,2)` ↔ minor-units boundary for patient invoices, via the string form and never `.toNumber()`

The finalisation check `branches.region_code` was always missing: a clinic registered in one state cannot issue from a branch in another, because `registrationFor()` would silently fall back to the wrong GSTIN

`loadInvoiceDocumentData()` — an invoice row assembled into the plain-JSON snapshot the document renders from. The ONE place an invoice becomes a document, so the preview and the PDF cannot be assembled differently
The snapshot beats the live row: a clinic that renames itself does not silently restate an invoice somebody is holding

What the document CALLS ITSELF is derived, not a constant — a Bill of Supply for an exempt Indian supply, a plain Invoice for an unregistered clinic, a Tax Invoice in AU/NZ/SG/AE and not in the UK or Ireland

`issueInvoice()` — finalise in a transaction, COMMIT, then enqueue the render. Enqueueing inside the transaction races the worker against the commit; a failed enqueue is logged and never fails the request, because by then the invoice IS a document
businessRules: A number is taken at finalisation, never at creation, so an abandoned draft burns no serial — enforced by the `invoices_number_matches_status` CHECK, not by a service remembering to
The series is per branch and the branch code is IN the number: two branches sharing one GSTIN must never issue the same serial
An invoice-level discount is apportioned onto the lines BEFORE tax, largest-remainder — tax on a pre-discount amount is over-collected tax remitted on money nobody received
Tax is rounded per line, not per invoice, which is what makes each printed line internally consistent
The customer block is a snapshot, not a join: a patient who changes their surname does not change an invoice already issued
An issued invoice is VOIDed, never deleted — the number stays so the series stays contiguous

An invoice's link to what it bills is enforced by the database, composite-keyed to (organization_id, id), so it can never cite another clinic's row; `invoices_source_reference_matches_type` keeps the source type and the reference column agreeing
A discount larger than what it reduces is REFUSED, never clamped: a negative charge is a credit note and goes through a different door
The invoice-level discount is weighted by what is LEFT of a line after its own discount, not by its gross — weighting by gross pushes an already-free line negative
One UNRATED or PROVIDER_REQUIRED line makes the whole document unissuable, decided by `isIssuable()` so the engine and finalisation cannot drift
The invoice tax total is summed from the PRINTED lines, never taken from a quote's own total — the lines are what a patient can add up on the page
An ISSUED invoice's document may not change — status, `amount_paid` and the cancel/void fields are the only columns that still move, enforced by trigger and not by the service
An issued invoice's LINES are frozen with it: a frozen `grand_total` over editable lines is an invoice stating a total that is not the sum of what it prints
CANCELLED is reachable from DRAFT only and VOID from an issued state only — the difference is whether anybody ever saw the document
A draft is re-priced at finalisation from its stored INPUTS, never trusted, so a rate corrected since the draft was opened reaches the document
limitations: Only APPOINTMENT has a reference column, because it is the only source whose table exists. PROCEDURE and SERVICE carry no reference at all until a service catalogue exists, and LAB / PHARMACY / INVENTORY gain theirs in the migration that creates their own table
No routes, no contracts, no screen and no permission wiring — phases 5 to 9
Lab, pharmacy and inventory sources have no tables to point at; only APPOINTMENT, PROCEDURE, SERVICE and OTHER can be billed
Tax behaviour is EXCLUSIVE only — there is no inclusive-pricing path, and `netOf()` in `@rcln/tax` has no caller. It matters for consumer-facing EU/UK prices

No credit note: no table, no series, no `CREDIT_NOTE` source type. A void records a reason and nothing else — and with no patient-payments table `amount_paid` is always zero, so no void can yet involve money
PARTIALLY_PAID and PAID are reachable transitions with nothing to drive them; there is no patient payments/allocations pair
Cash rounding and the invoice currency are parameters, not settings — `resolveSettings()` has no billing keys and Phase 7's settings screen is where they belong
No routes, no contracts, no screen and no permission wiring — phases 6 to 9. `billing.invoice.*` still gates nothing
The PDF is asynchronous: an invoice is ISSUED before its document exists. The screen renders from data so nothing waits to SEE the invoice — only Download waits

name: Inventory
purpose: Where a thing IS and how much of it there is. The other half of the product catalogue, which has no quantity anywhere in it. One engine for medicines, consumables, devices, implants, reagents and dental materials — PI-2 of the pharmacy-inventory programme.
features: `stock_ledger` — append-only, and the ONLY source of quantity truth (PI-ADR-004). Enforced by two independent layers: `rcln_app` holds no UPDATE or DELETE on it, and a trigger refuses both anyway
`stock_balances` — a CACHE maintained by a SECURITY DEFINER trigger. `rcln_app` holds no INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE on it at all, so "nothing writes the cache" is a grant rather than an agreement

`recordMovement()` in `@rcln/inventory` — the single writer. In a PACKAGE because the expiry sweep runs in the worker, and an application-local writer would have forced the worker to write its own INSERT
The caller never chooses a sign: `movement_type` decides it, and `stock_ledger_direction` CHECKs the pairing plus which status buckets the row may name
Every movement converts to the product's BASE UNIT through `assertExactConversion`, which refuses an inexact conversion rather than rounding it
`inventory_locations` / `storage_areas` / `storage_bins` — branch → location → area → bin (PI-ADR-012). A branch has MANY locations; assuming one is unrecoverable without a migration under live stock
`batches` — lot, expiry, retest, cost per BASE unit in integer minor units, plus the recall and quarantine columns (the workflow is PI-10)
`serials` — one physically identifiable device. `assigned_patient_id` is PHI and every read of it writes a `data_access_logs` row under the new `INVENTORY_SERIAL` resource
`verifyBalances()` — replays the ledger in SQL and compares it with the cache. It REPORTS and never repairs: a cache that heals itself hides the trigger bug that broke it

The expiry sweep — moves AVAILABLE → EXPIRED on the day, in the BRANCH's timezone, resolved as `(now() AT TIME ZONE b.timezone)::date` in SQL. Idempotent by construction, not by a `last_swept_at` column

`inventory_branches_with_expired_stock()` — the sweep's one cross-tenant question, a SECURITY DEFINER function returning three ids for only the branches that are due. Twin of `billing_due_subscriptions`
Four screens under `/stock`: overview (what needs doing, then what is where), lots, locations and the movement ledger
userActions: See what is on each shelf, and what is expiring
Record a lot when stock of a batch-tracked product arrives
Adjust, return, damage, dispose, hold or release stock — each as a movement with a reason
Put a lot on hold or recall it, which moves its quantity and sets its status in one transaction
Read the movement ledger: what moved, when, from where to where, and who did it
businessRules: Nothing outside `recordMovement()` inserts into `stock_ledger`; nothing at all writes `stock_balances`
A correction is a COMPENSATING MOVEMENT with a reason, never an edit
`stock_balances` disagreeing with a ledger replay is a bug in the trigger, and the LEDGER WINS
Only `AVAILABLE` is allocatable. Everything else is visible, countable and valued but not dispensable — which is exactly why quarantine works

EXPIRY, DAMAGE and RECALL MOVE quantity between buckets rather than removing it: expired stock is on the shelf, undispensable, and has to be counted until it is destroyed. DISPOSAL is the one that records a physical departure
ADJUSTMENT is the only movement that requires a reason code — the only one whose meaning is not stated by its name, and where shrinkage hides

A batch's status and its quantity move in ONE transaction: a lot flagged QUARANTINED whose stock is still in the AVAILABLE bucket is dispensable, because allocation reads the balance and not the batch
Near-expiry produces an ALERT and never a status change. Only the sweep, on the day itself, moves anything
Alert windows are SETTINGS (`inventory.expiry_alert_days`), not constants (PI-ADR-015)
The tracking mode is enforced in the DATABASE: a SERIAL product moving without a serial is refused by a CHECK, not only by a service (PI-ADR-014)
Lot uniqueness is tenant- AND branch-qualified: a lot number is the manufacturer's, and one group receiving that lot at two sites holds it twice, at two costs
limitations: `POST /v1/stock/movements` accepts only the MANUAL movement types. Dispensing (PI-7) must consult the regulatory engine first, consumption is PI-9, transfers are PI-3 and are only ever written as a PAIR in one transaction, and goods receipts are PI-4
`RESERVED` and `IN_TRANSIT` are real statuses with no workflow behind them yet — reservations are PI-3.4 and in-transit transfers are PI-3.3
No FEFO allocation service. The data supports it (batches are indexed by expiry, and `inventory.batch_selection_strategy` is already a setting) but nothing allocates — PI-3.5
No screens for CREATING a location, a lot or a movement: the four screens read. The write surface exists on the API and is exercised by tests
Recall and quarantine COLUMNS exist and the hold endpoint works; the recall WORKFLOW — affected-stock queries, blocked dispensing, traceability reports — is PI-10
No costing beyond `batches.unit_cost_base`: no moving average, no valuation, no aging. PI-4.8 and PI-22

The worker's `MovementDeps` binding is a second implementation of `recordAudit` and `loadUnitGraph`, written against `@rcln/db` directly because the worker cannot import the API's. Nothing catches the two drifting
